title: Unit econ one-pager: quick calc and tier sketches
content:
Purpose: quick back-of-envelope (BOE) to sanity-check per-session and per-token pricing levers. Use this as a fast reference for convo bundling, starter credits, and microcommit tiers. Not final — lots of assumptions.

Assumptions (baseline model/workload)
- Model: 13B dense quantized (8-bit), typical interactive load.
- Equivalent throughput: ~60 tokens/sec peak per GPU for gen path (in our infra profile).
- Avg session length: 450 tokens (roundtrip prompt + response; includes system + few messages).
- Avg concurrency per tenant under peak: 3 sessions.
- Effective GPU util: 65% (scheduling + idle gaps + KV reuse).
- Cloud cost proxy: $3.5/GPU-hour (amortized infra + ops for shared hosting), Dedicated bucket ~ $9/GPU-hour.

Derived primitives
- Tokens per hour per GPU (theoretical peak): 60 tps * 3600 = 216k tokens/hr. With util 65% => ~140k tokens/hr.
- Cost per token (shared): $3.5 / 140k ≈ $0.000025 per token (~0.0025 cents).
- Cost per session (tokens): 450 * $0.000025 ≈ $0.01125 (~1.1 cents) raw infra.
- Add 30% ops/overhead (network, storage, requests): session opex => 1.1c * 1.3 ≈ 1.43 cents.
- Add margins, support, metering → list price per session (x4 markup) ≈ 5.7 cents.

Implications for pricing levers
1) Pay-as-you-go token price: to hit >3x gross margin vs shared infra, list token price ~0.00008–0.0001 ($0.00008/token ⇒ $0.036/session).  This leaves room for discounts and credits.
2) Session bundles: sell 100-session pack for SMB at $2.50 (2.5c/session) — loses money on pure infra for casual workloads unless we assume microbatching and higher cache hit rates. Good for acquisition.
3) Starter credit sizing: $20 credit equals ~560 sessions at $0.036/session list price — good friction reducer.
4) Dedicated/reserved: customers who commit can get 35–60% off list; still profitable if utilization >70% because their effective cost per token drops (economies of scale + GPU scheduling efficiency).

Edge considerations (things to model next)
- Prefix caching: for retrieval/chat with repeated system tokens, effective session tokens drop 15–40% for second+ calls — credit worthiness changes.
- Short convo pathology (microinteractions): 30–80 token sessions have high relative overhead => consider flat per-call minimum or small per-call surcharge.
- Latency-sensitive premium: add 10–25% surcharge for low-latency SLA routes (hot path + dedicated pool routing).
- Minimal-commit tiers: allow 100–500 session monthly commit with auto-topup; price anchoring at ~60% of payg to nudge commitments.

Sketch pricing tiers (quick)
- Free / dev: 100 sessions/mo free (mild friction), then payg.
- Starter: $19/mo — includes 500 sessions + 30k tokens of embeddings (baked). Effective list PS: 3.8c/session. Encourages mid-frequency users.
- Pro: $199/mo — includes 7,000 sessions + 200k embed units; includes 48-hour retention of logs and 1 dev seat. Effective per-session ~2.8c.
- Dedicated: custom pricing, baseline commit $5k/mo — target 50% discount off list for steady utilization.

Unit tests to run next (not done)
- Recompute per-token cost with 70B quantized (lower throughput -> cost/token up x3).
- Add embedding hotpaths: embedding compute cost per vector vs gen tokens — map to composite sku.
- Model mix: 40% cheap queries (summaries), 40% medium, 20% heavy (long context) -> blended unit econ.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Do we price by session (easy to market) or tokens (precise unit econ)? Short sessions favor session pricing; long context favors token pricing. Hybrid might be necessary.
- Should we offer per-route latency premiums or bake into tiered SLOs? Simpler to offer two SKUs: standard & low-latency.
- Credit decay: how long should starter credits be valid? 6 months vs 12 months materially affects breakage metrics.

Quick simulation (hand calc)
- If 10k active starter users churn 5%/mo and use 20 sessions/mo each -> gross sessions = 2M/mo. At list 3.6c/session => $72k/mo revenue. If avg blended cost 1.4c/session -> gross margin ~61%. Useful sanity check.

Next actions (me)
- Run exact per-token throughput numbers from infra team for 13B/70B quantized profiles (ticket: PR-3251).
- Build a micro-sim (spreadsheet) that samples session length distribution (short/mid/long) and outputs blended cost & recommended list price bands.
- Draft starter credit expirations and experimentation matrix.

Notes-to-self: keep pricing language simple for landing pages, show concrete examples ("500 sessions = X chats for an app"), and avoid exposing token math to end-users except in advanced docs.

References: link to infra perf spreadsheet, Confluence pricing notes (see linked_artifacts).

End of one-pager BOE.
